response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), s AS (SELECT gender, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT gender, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT gender, cnt AS invoice_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Genders are taken as the distinct values of Customers.gender among linked invoices; a NULL gender, if present, forms its own group and counts as a gender in the average.
Each invoice is counted once via Invoices -> Orders -> Customers inner joins (no join to line items, so invoices are not duplicated).
